A.notes: Cannot find the file and asks for the path, even providing the exact workspace directory. No over-engineering, no premature framework. Maximally proportional given a missing file.

B.notes: Asks for the file/contents and references the actual task (sum the amount column), confirming it understood the request. Simple, no infrastructure proposed.

C.notes: Notes the missing file and asks to confirm path or upload/create it. Concise and proportional, but slightly more generic than B which echoed the actual column-sum task.

analysis: All three systems behaved identically and correctly: the target file does not exist, so none of them attempted to write code at all, let alone an over-engineered CSV framework with pandas, argparse, or error handling. This makes all three maximally proportional and they earn top marks across every criterion. Differences are marginal and concern only the quality of the clarifying question. B edges ahead by restating the actual intent ('parse it and sum the amount column'), demonstrating it grasped the task before asking. A is also strong, giving the precise workspace path to make it easy for the user to drop the file. C is functionally equivalent but the most generic of the three. Since the proportionality rubric measures resistance to over-engineering, all three are effectively tied at the ceiling; the ranking reflects only the slight edge in helpfulness of the clarifying prompt.
